html:
Irish republican armed group that fought to end British rule in Northern Ireland and unite Ireland, from 1969 to its ceasefires and end of the campaign in 2005.

It formed in December 1969 and January 1970 when the old Irish Republican Army split. Younger members, angry that it had not defended Catholic areas during the riots of that August, broke away as the "Provisionals". The old group became the Official IRA.

The Provisionals ran a long campaign of bombings and shootings against the British Army, police, and economic targets in Northern Ireland and England. It killed about 1,700 people in all, many of them civilians, as in Bloody Friday. Its political side, Sinn Fein, gained votes after the 1981 hunger strike.

It declared a ceasefire in 1994, ended it in 1996, and called another in 1997. It backed the Good Friday Agreement and in 2005 ordered an end to armed action and put its weapons beyond use. See the-troubles for the wider conflict.
sum: Irish republican armed group that fought to end British rule in Northern Ireland and unite Ireland, from 1969 to its ceasefires and end of the campaign in 2005.
